what: The heuristic precomputes customer visited/location facts and reconstructs the depot/customer routing matrix from grounded `visit` and `return-to-depot` operator costs. At evaluation it identifies the current location and unvisited customers, then computes the maximum of an MST routing relaxation and a route-degree bound. When exact `capacity()`, `demand(customer)`, and `load()` PNEs are available, it estimates the minimum number of remaining routes and increases the required depot degree accordingly. Missing resource PNEs are handled permissively, leaving the routing relaxation active.
why: CVRP states differ primarily by the current endpoint, remaining customers, and available route capacity. MST and degree relaxations capture the dominant geometric cost of connecting all remaining customers and returning to the depot while remaining inexpensive for the representative instance sizes. The capacity-aware depot-degree term addresses the many-small-capacity instances where several depot trips are unavoidable, while exact operator-cost reconstruction avoids unsafe dependence on folded travel-cost expressions. The design remains useful on instances where capacity and demand names have been eliminated by translation.
